subject: Banking
title: Credit Card Interest Is King
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Credit Card Interest Is King.

hook.text: The average credit card interest rate is 24%. That makes credit cards the most profitable lending product in banking.

buildup.text: Americans carry $1.1 trillion in credit card debt. At 24% interest, that generates over $260 billion in annual interest.

discovery.text: Banks fund credit card loans with deposits at 0.5%. The spread between 0.5% and 24% is enormous profit per dollar lent.

twist.text: Only half of cardholders carry a balance. The other half use cards for free and earn rewards.

climax.text: Credit cards are the most profitable bank product because the interest rate is high and customers rarely question it.

punchline.text: 24% interest on $1.1 trillion in debt. Credit cards are banking's gold mine.

quiz.question: What is the average credit card interest rate in the US?

details.summary: Credit card interest is the single largest revenue source for many banks, with average APRs exceeding 20 percent on revolving balances. Americans pay over $100 billion annually in credit card interest, making it the most profitable bank product.
details.whyItMatters: Credit card interest rates are among the highest consumers face. Understanding how banks profit from revolving balances reveals why the industry aggressively markets cards and sets minimum payments deceptively low.
takeaways: Average credit card APR exceeds 20 percent, far above other loan types
Americans carry over $1 trillion in revolving credit card debt
Minimum payments are designed to maximize interest collection over time

faq.question: Why are credit card interest rates so much higher than other loans?
faq.answer: Credit cards are unsecured debt with no collateral for the bank to seize if you default. The higher rate compensates for this risk. However, the high rate combined with minimum payments means banks earn far more from cards than their risk justifies.

faq.question: How do minimum payments maximize bank profits?
faq.answer: A minimum payment of 2 percent on a $5,000 balance at 20 percent APR would take over 30 years to repay and cost over $8,000 in interest. Banks set minimums low to keep balances revolving as long as possible.
